title: Pauri 8, sound: suniai
tomorrow: Pauri 8, meaning: the power of listening

segments.voice: Yesterday, nadar, and the turn of pauri seven: famous for ages, and still, without the glance, no one asks after you. Your line was fame is not it.

If you've ever sat in a gurdwara at dawn while Japji is recited, there's a stretch where one word rolls around and around the room like a wave coming in. It's a soft word, almost a sigh, and once you've heard it you'll hear it all through this part of Japji, because for four pauris straight it starts nearly every line. At the start of this camp, i said Japji would give four whole pauris to one word. Today that word arrives.
screen: `A WAVE COMING IN.` → `A SOFT WORD, ALMOST A SIGH.` → `FOUR PAURIS FOR ONE WORD.`

segments.voice: The word is suniai: SUN-i-ai. The first syllable is like soon, but short, closer to the u in put. Then a light i. Then ai, a little like the start of air. The n in the middle, in Gurmukhi, is the one made with the tongue curled back, the same n you heard at the end of taan in pauri three. Suniai comes from sunnaa, to hear, to listen, and the ending means something like by, or through. By listening. Through hearing. Pauri eight opens: suniai sidh peer sur naath. Sidh: siddhas, yogis said to have gained great powers. Peer: pirs, the Sufi masters, the spiritual guides of Muslim Punjab. Sur: the gods. Naath: the naths, masters of a yogic order; the stories of Guru Nanak's travels have him meeting and talking with them. In one breath, the line names holy people of many kinds from Guru Nanak's world, and says they came to be what they are by listening. Now the rhythm. Pauri eight: suniai, suniai, suniai. Pauris nine, ten and eleven, the same: line after line opening on one soft word, a drumbeat Japji keeps going for four whole pauris. And every one of the four ends on the same two lines, a refrain about devotees being always in bloom. That opens tomorrow.
screen: `SUNIAI — BY LISTENING.` · `SIDH, PEER, SUR, NAATH.` · `HOLY PEOPLE OF MANY KINDS.` · `FOUR PAURIS, ONE DRUMBEAT.` · then, large: `SUNIAI.`

segments.voice: Say the word slowly, five times, with a breath between each one: suniai. Then stop speaking and do what the word says: listen to the room, the street, your own breath, the small hum of whatever machine is nearby, naming nothing, just receiving it. If you pray, you can let Waheguru be the last sound before the quiet.
Suniai. By listening. The soft word that opens nearly every line of Japji's pauris eight to eleven.
Your line: suniai, listening. For today, one word is enough. Day one hundred seventy-seven, done.

howItsDone: Pauris eight to eleven of Japji, each line beginning suniai, are part of the morning recitation; together they are Japji's stretch on listening to the Name.
